turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I'll just do your observations before Doctor Naidoo sees you. Have a seat this side.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning. Thank you, I appreciate it.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure today is one oh nine over seventy-seven. Your last pressure was one-forty.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I see. It is lower than it was.

[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Temperature is thirty-eight point three, pulse is seventy-six, and the weight, err, I first read fifty-eight, sorry, it's fifty-two kilograms. Last time in March you were sixty-eight.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. I have been quite deliberate about the weight since March. I cut back on bread, and I walk at lunch.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): Lovely. That's me done. The doctor will be through now-now.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good morning, I'm Doctor Naidoo. What brings you in today?

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning, Doctor. I have come about pain in my lower back that shoots down my left leg. It has been three weeks, it began after I helped my brother move a couch, and when I sit it is six out of ten.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. What eases it, if anything?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): If I stand and walk about, it eases somewhat. Sitting is by far the worst.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm. And your work?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): I am an accountant, Doctor, at a desk most of the day in Rosebank.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any numbness, tingling, or weakness in that leg?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. Nothing of that sort.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Waterworks and bowels, any change, or numbness in the saddle area?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Those have been entirely normal. And there is no weakness in the leg, if I may be precise.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): What have you been using for the pain?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): I take ibuprophen tablets by mouth for this back pain, four hundred milligrams, three times a day, with food. It takes the edge off, though it does not clear it.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ibuprofen, yes. Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No, none that I am aware of.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): I ought to mention, umm, as well, that a colleague, Mrs Dlamini, advised cobra stretches. I have been doing them in the evenings.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thank you. Have you felt feverish, or unwell in yourself?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I have not felt feverish.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Just the other systems, quickly. Cardiovascular, anything at all?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. The heart side has been quite fine.

[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me summarise. Three weeks of lower back pain shooting into the left leg, six out of ten with sitting, better if you walk, and ibuprofen four hundred milligrams three times a day helps a little. No leg weakness, waterworks and bowels normal, and you have deliberately come down from sixty-eight kilograms in March to fifty-two. Temperature today is thirty-eight point three, though you do not feel feverish, and the pressure is one oh nine over seventy-seven, previously one-forty.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): That is correct, Doctor. Thank you.

[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Onto the couch, please. There is tenderness over the lower lumbar spine, and straight leg raise on the left brings on the leg pain at forty degrees. The right leg comes up fully with no pain. Power is normal in both legs, and the ankle reflexes are present.

[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Forgive me, Doctor, I need to correct myself. Well, actually, there is a tingling, pins and needles, in the left foot when I sit for a long while. I should not have said there was none.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am glad you came back to it. So pins and needles are present in the left foot after prolonged sitting. Still no weakness.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. That is accurate. No weakness.

[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): My working impression is a left lumbar nerve root irritation, sciatica, mechanical. The temperature is a slight concern, but you look well and the pattern fits a nerve, so I am not arranging a scan today.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand. I would be grateful to hear the plan.

[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am referring you to physiotherapy. Please stop those cobra stretches until the physio has assessed you, they can stir the nerve. Carry on with the ibuprofen, four hundred milligrams three times a day with food, and stand up at least every half an hour.

[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): I will see you again in six weeks. If it has not settled by then, we might arrange a scan, but not before. Should the leg go weak, or you cannot pass urine, or the numbness reaches the saddle area, come back at once, or go to casualty.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, Doctor. I will do exactly that. I shall also ask my medical aid about the physio.
[SEG0038] person_1 (NURSE): Right. I'll book the physio and the six-week visit at the desk.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): That is very kind. Thank you both.

spec.situation: Person with low back pain shooting down one leg for three weeks, worse sitting; takes ibuprofen; a colleague's advice on exercises; doctor examines straight-leg raise and plans physio, no scan yet.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

features: spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

omissions.text: Ibuprofen is to be taken with food.
Last recorded weight in March was 68 kg, and the doctor noted the drop from 68 kg to 52 kg was deliberate.

Negative finding initially given for numbness/tingling was later corrected by the patient; there is tingling/pins and needles in the left foot after prolonged sitting, so the earlier denial should not stand unqualified.
Right straight leg raise was full with no pain.
The doctor stated he is not arranging a scan today.
Return immediately or go to casualty also if saddle-area numbness develops; this was part of the safety-net advice.
